title: Collect every VCF Operations log agent group in stable order
prompt:
Complete `vcf_ops_logs/client.py` as a standard-library-only Python package for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 VCF Operations Log Management.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused REST contract was projected directly from `specifications/vcf-operations/log-management-openapi.json` in the Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable commit recorded in both files. The JSON OpenAPI specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly operationId `getAllAgentGroupConfig` on `GET /api/v2/agent/groups`; contact no other route.

Preserve the public imports in `vcf_ops_logs/__init__.py` and the existing signatures in `vcf_ops_logs/client.py`. Implement `LogManagementClient(base_url, token, *, timeout=5.0)` and `list_all_agent_groups(*, page_size=100) -> list[AgentGroup]`. The method must retrieve every page, buffer the complete collection, and return immutable `AgentGroup` values sorted by `name` and then `id` using Python's case-sensitive Unicode code-point ordering. Page boundaries and server item order must not affect output order.

The OpenAPI `pageable` query object uses the OpenAPI 3.0 defaults `style=form` and `explode=true`. Start at zero and send exactly `page=<n>&size=<page_size>` in that order. Increment `page` by one until the returned `Page.last` is true. The optional `Pageable.sort` field is unset for this operation: omit it entirely rather than sending an empty string, repeated empty value, JSON, null, or a default. Never append a bare `?`.

Every request is a bodyless GET with exactly one `X-JWT-Token` header and `Accept: application/json`. Do not send `Authorization`, `Content-Type`, `Content-Length`, or a transfer-encoded body. Require exactly HTTP 200 and JSON. Raise `ApiError` for HTTP or transport failures and `ResponseContractError` for a malformed success response.

The specification models the response as an array of `Page` objects. In this focused contract, require exactly one page object per response. Validate `content`, `empty`, `first`, `last`, `number`, `numberOfElements`, `size`, `totalElements`, and `totalPages`; require the requested page number and size, consistent totals, correct Boolean flags, monotonic progress, and a final buffered count equal to `totalElements`. Reject early or contradictory completion, duplicate nonblank string `id` values across pages, and malformed content items. Each item must have a nonblank string `id`, a nonblank string `name`, Boolean `autoUpdate`, and string `info`. Map only those values to `AgentGroup(id, name, auto_update, info)`. Do not return partial data after a later-page failure.

Validation must occur before traffic. `base_url` must be an absolute HTTP(S) origin with no credentials, non-root path, query, or fragment. `token` must be a nonblank CR/LF-free string. `timeout` must be a finite positive non-Boolean number. `page_size` must be a non-Boolean integer from 1 through 1000. Errors must not expose the token or raw response bodies.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port and reads its in-memory request log. The mock derives its complete method/path allow-list from `docs/contract.json`, serves only the named operation, generates the token and group identities at runtime, and returns three pages. A second inventory call uses different page membership and item order for the same collection. Verification asserts complete retrieval, stable ordering, exact ordered methods and raw targets, header multiplicity, zero-byte bodies, omission of `sort` and every empty optional value, no extra calls, error behavior, and standard-library-only imports. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `pyproject.toml` and `vcf_ops_logs/__init__.py`, is protected. Edit only `vcf_ops_logs/client.py`. Do not add dependencies or require package installation.
scenario: the agent-group collection spans three pages whose membership and item order change between otherwise identical complete inventory calls
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves complete zero-based pagination and total omission of the unset Pageable.sort member
